notes.title: Patch 1.1.07
notes.notes:
[b]Additions and Changes:[/b]

[list]
[*] Added a save data backup system. Every time you quit the game from the main menu, the game will save a backup version of your save data. In the event of data corruption due to power loss or other unexpected happenings, the game will detect the corruption and auto-restore from the backup save data. This change will not negatively affect existing save data.
[/list]

notes.notes: Just tweaking a glowing material that was not, in fact, glowing.

notes.notes:
[b]Bugs Fixed:[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the power switch required to exit the Xugan Caverns would sometimes not spawn in the correct location.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.03
notes.notes:
Bugs Fixed:

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where going into a challenge ticket level would set the current climb checkpoint incorrectly, resulting in incorrect climb progress.
[*] Fixed an issue where navigating with a gamepad/controller on the main menu got stuck on the Discord button when going downwards.
[*] Fixed an issue where blocks caught in level geometry would sometimes get launched down into the terrain.
[*] Fixed an issue where sometimes pickup block culling distance was too short, resulting in very close pop-in.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Update
notes.notes:
Hello all,

Xaeveax (Alex) here. I'm the developer of [b]Ocnus Theory[/b]. It's been in development for a few years now and is finally reaching the finish line. I've been developing it part-time on the side of my full time job, so it's taken longer than perhaps it should have. 

This will be the first proper dev update I've done for the game, as it's largely been developed in isolation and secrecy. I've tried to keep things pretty close to the chest until the game was ready to release, and I can confidently say that the time is approaching shortly, hopefully by the end of the year. I am hoping for an August release window but it will largely depend on how QA testing goes.

As for actual development, I'm wrapping things up and putting the finishing touches on everything. [b]The game itself is 95% finished.[/b] I'm in the QA testing phase, which is proving to be quite time consuming as a single, part-time developer. That said, things are coming along nicely and it's getting more and more polished with each play test. 

I'm hoping to start posting little tidbits of info about the game leading up to it's release, going over things like mechanics, locations, features, and maybe even some insight behind the development curtains. This will likely be here on Steam, though a future community Discord channel will be the place for more in-depth discussion. 

Some of the main things I'll be working on in the following weeks and months include:

[list]
[*][b]Play testing the game[/b] many times and fixing any bugs I encounter.
[*][b]Polishing up a few of the ability mechanics.[/b] These are unlocked as you progress, and some of the late-game ones really change up the game. I just need to make sure they work nicely across all locations.
[*][b]Finishing up the lore notes.[/b] The game is focused on the gameplay, but the story/lore of the world does have quite a bit of [b]depth[/b] to it and I need to make sure it's all communicated properly.
[*][b]Challenge Mode polish.[/b] Some of the bonus challenge mode levels need a bit of love still, as they were built before some of the new ability mechanics were introduced.
[*] [b]Sound effects work.[/b] Currently, the sounds played when dropping blocks, moving around, bumping into surfaces, etc. are all a bit unsatisfying. Due to the physics-driven nature of the game, designing the sounds for all of these interactions to take context into account takes more time than one might expect.
[*] [b]Portable checkpoint bugfixing. [/b] The portable checkpoint flag system works great, but there are a few things about them that need some serious special attention. It's a pretty important feature in the game, letting you place your own checkpoints [i](nearly)[/i] anywhere you want, so I want to make sure they function properly in all contexts.
[*] [b]Performance on lower-end machines.[/b] The game runs buttery smooth on higher-end PCs, but lower end cards (testing on a GTX960 for example) proves to have some undesirable slowdown when on max settings. Of course, this can be solved by simply turning down some of the graphic options, but ideally I would like as many people as possible to be able to play it at 60 FPS. Despite the deceptively simple art style, the game does take advantage of lots of dynamic lights and precise physics, both of which take their toll in certain locations.
[/list]

I'll try to keep things updated on here as I get closer to release. I'm also in the middle of setting up a community Discord server, which will be primarily for hearing feedback and discussing the game. I plan to continue to update the game post-release to improve it and add features that might be requested, so having a Discord will be a helpful tool to keep us all connected in that way.
